name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Apply a 7-day hard decay to every prompt in the system, no exceptions.

This forces stale prompts out fast, keeping the engine lean and relevant. The trade-off is losing some prompt history, but that’s a feature—old prompts clog the system and mislead routing.

name: Gauge
text: A 7-day hard decay risks losing context critical for routing—some prompts only trigger in rare edge cases, and their absence could force the engine into brittle fallbacks. Instead, test a rolling 30-day weighted decay with a 15% floor: it prunes stale prompts gradually while preserving rare but valuable signals. The argument settles when we compare routing accuracy before/after on a held-out set of edge-case prompts.

name: Gauge
text: A 7-day hard decay guarantees losing prompts that only fire in rare edge cases—those aren’t noise, they’re the exact signals routing depends on. Instead, test a 14-day rolling decay with a 10% floor: it prunes stale prompts faster than 30 days while keeping rare triggers alive longer than 7 days. Settle it with a 30-day A/B test: measure routing accuracy and prompt retention for both decays before committing.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Adopt a 14-day rolling decay with a 10% floor for all prompts—faster than 30 days, slower than 7, preserving rare edge-case triggers while pruning stale noise.

Result: A pruned prompt set with no hard 7-day cuts, keeping routing stable. Owner: Gauge (improve-checker) delivers the decay system and confirms the artifact exists.
